summary: The list of every language the game ships with. A GameDataRegistry<LocaleAsset> and nothing more.
overview: The single asset you hand LocalizationManager. It holds every LocaleAsset, and looking a language up by its code is the base class's own GetById — there is no code in this file at all beyond the [CreateAssetMenu] line, which is the point: GameDataRegistry<T> already solved this, and a language keyed by a locale code is exactly the shape it solves.
useCases: Giving the manager one reference instead of a list of language assets.
Adding a language to a shipped game by dropping its asset into this list.
Keeping a language out of a build by removing it here, without deleting its asset.

gotchas.title: The registry is the only place the manager looks
gotchas.body: A LocaleAsset that exists in the project but is not listed here does not exist as far as the game is concerned. This is the most common reason a language you just imported does not show up.

gotchas.title: Create it via the importer, not by hand, unless you want to wire it yourself
gotchas.body: Toolkit > Localization Importer creates the registry and fills it as part of an import. Assets > Create > Toolkit > Localization > Locale Registry makes an empty one you then populate by dragging.

walkthrough.group: Inherited from GameDataRegistry<LocaleAsset> — this asset declares no fields of its own
walkthrough.name: Entries
walkthrough.what: ORDER MATTERS in two places: AvailableLocaleCodes returns this order, so it is the order a language picker will show; and first-run system-language detection scans it top to bottom, so the first matching locale wins. An empty slot or a duplicate code is warned about and skipped, not thrown on. A re-import appends new languages and never reorders or removes existing ones.
